answer.effective_date: Effective December 1, 2025; Last Review October 2025; Next Review December 2026
criteria_quotes: I. Rotator cuff repair may be considered medically necessary when all of the following Criteria are met (A.-D.):
A. Documentation of function-limiting pain (e.g., loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out activities of daily living and/or demands of employment); and

B. Either of the following criteria are met: 1. Failure to respond to at least three months of non-surgical management which includes documentation of physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program and one or more of the following unless contraindicated: a. Trial of anti-inflammatory medication; or b. Cortisone injection; or 2. The individual suffers from a discrete traumatic event that results in an acute full-thickness rotator cuff tear and has associated function limiting pain; and

C. Individual meets all of the following Criteria (1. and 2.) on physical examination when compared to the non-involved side: 1. Either of the following: a. Functionally limited active range of motion; or b. Measurable loss of strength of the rotator cuff musculature; and 2. One or more of the following positive orthopedic tests/signs: a. Drop Arm Test; or b. Painful Arc Test; or c. Jobe or Empty Can Test; or d. External Rotation Lag Sign (Dropping Sign); or e. Internal Rotation Lag Sign; or f. Lift-Off Test; or g. Bear Hug Test; or h. Belly-Press Test (Napoleon); or i. Belly-Off Test; or j. Neer Impingement Test; or k. Hawkins-Kennedy Impingement; or l. Hornblower Test (Patte); and

D. Advanced diagnostic imaging study (e.g., MRI, CT) demonstrates a partial-thickness rotator cuff tear or a full-thickness rotator cuff tear that correlates with the individual's reported symptoms and physical exam findings.
answer.appeal_deadline: 180 days from the date of the denial notice (2026-08-22), i.e., by 2027-02-18, as stated in the denial letter. This is consistent with the standard internal-appeal window described in Washington's Office of the Insurance Commissioner consumer appeals guide for individual/commercial ACA plans.
answer.submission_route: I could not verify, from a public source specific to this member's exact Regence BlueShield Washington commercial/ACA plan, the current mailing address, fax number, or online portal Regence uses for MEMBER (as opposed to provider) medical-necessity appeals. answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The medical-necessity criteria quoted above come from a publicly hosted copy of Regence's Medical Policy Manual, Surgery Policy No. 228 'Shoulder Surgeries,' which a third-party policy-tracking service (policyalerts.com) also confirms is tracked as a Regence BCBS commercial medical policy. To be certain this is the exact version Regence applied to this specific denial, the patient (or their provider) should: (1) call the customer service number on the back of the Regence member ID card or in the denial letter and ask for the specific medical policy number and version cited in the review, (2) request a free copy of the criteria and the reviewer's rationale — insurers are required to provide the specific rules, guidelines, or clinical review criteria relied on when requested, per ACA internal claims and appeals regulations (29 CFR 2590.715-2719 / 45 CFR 147.136) — and (3) check Regence's public provider policy library at https://www.regence.com/provider/library/policies-guidelines/medical-policy (this page requires a browser session/JS to search by policy name or ID; it was not retrievable via a plain HTTP fetch in this session).
